title: Prepare and check the trial balance
goal: Build a trial balance from ledger balances and distinguish arithmetic agreement from accounting accuracy.

slides.title: The trial balance summarizes account balances
slides.takeaway: The trial balance is an internal working report.
slides.notes: It is not one of the four financial statements.

slides.title: Use ending balances rather than transaction totals
slides.takeaway: Carry $8,840 to the Cash trial balance line.
slides.notes: Include opening balances in other datasets. Summit Trail starts at zero.

slides.title: Place each balance in the debit or credit column
slides.takeaway: Each nonzero account balance normally appears in one column.
slides.notes: This excerpt does not balance on its own. Use the actual balance side; investigate unexpected signs.

slides.title: Build a trial balance from the teaching ledger
slides.lead: Summit Trail Co. · Trial balance · June 30 · USD
slides.takeaway: Every balance comes from the ledger.
slides.notes: All 17 nonzero balances appear. Beginning Retained Earnings is zero; no closing entries have been made. Revenue, expense, and dividend accounts therefore remain separate.

slides.title: Check debit and credit totals

items: Use the same accounts and reporting date.
Review missing accounts and unusual balances.

slides.takeaway: Agreement is an arithmetic check, not proof of accuracy.

slides.title: Trace an imbalance through the workflow

items.heading: Compare
items.text: Match trial balance lines to ledger balances.

slides.takeaway: Locate the cause before changing records.
slides.notes: Divisibility by nine can suggest a transposition, but is only a clue. Never use a plug account to force equality.

slides.title: Some errors leave the trial balance balanced

rows: Debit Equipment instead of Rent Expense
The wrong debit equals the credit

slides.takeaway: Check completeness and classification as well as equality.

slides.title: Try it: diagnose omission and misclassification

items.heading: Error A
items.text: A $200 utilities debit is posted; the payable credit is missing.

items.heading: Error B
items.text: A $600 equipment purchase is recorded as Rent Expense and Cash.

slides.notes: For B, debit Equipment and credit Rent Expense if using a documented correcting entry. Preserve the correction history; do not correct twice.

rows: Credits are $200 too low. Post the missing payable credit.
Totals agree. Move $600 from Rent Expense to Equipment.

slides.title: Check completeness before making statements

items: All source events are accounted for.
Unexpected accounts and signs are explained.
Known errors have been corrected and traced.

slides.takeaway: Start statements from a checked trial balance.
slides.notes: Assignment scope: no adjusting entries, adjusted trial balance, or closing entries. Fuller accrual reporting may require depreciation, estimates, and timing adjustments. This exercise does not claim full compliance with every standard.
